claims.text: The driver's own telemetry defeats his claim: the longest continuous in-geofence hold the trace credits is 236 seconds, open at 07:44:14 and closed by his cancellation at 07:48:10, against the 300 second minimum dwelling time for a TRANSPORT_HUB pickup — a shortfall of 64 seconds. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails on the record, and where that limb fails the fee is not chargeable under the clause.

The 'more than ten minutes' the driver asserts is measured from his 07:38:05 'arrived' marker, and POL-NS-01(c) expressly measures dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' event. The derived arrival block records dwell_start_offset_sec of -369 against that marker, and the run the policy credits opens at 07:44:14 — exactly 369 seconds after the marker. On the policy's clock the driver held his position for 236 seconds, not ten minutes, and the trip record's wait_time_min of 10.1 is measured from a marker the policy does not accept as starting the clock.

Limb (b) is not met either. The trace yields 25 qualifying in-radius fixes, and those are exactly the 25 fixes of the single 07:44:14–07:48:10 run (qualifying_fix_count equals that run's fix_count), so there is no qualifying in-radius fix at or before the 07:38:05 arrived event the marker depends on. On either reading the answer is the same: the driver was inside the pickup geofence for 236 seconds at the most.

Because the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the 300 second minimum for this zone class, POL-NS-06 governs the outcome: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, and no driver compensation is payable on this branch.

Nor can the driver close the 64 second gap by accumulation. The trace shows a single in-geofence interval in which he held position (run_count 1), so POL-NS-06(i) has no second interval to add to the first; and the traffic_advisory that limb (i) also requires is absent — EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload, so there is nothing to establish that holding position was not lawfully possible. POL-NS-06(ii) confirms an advisory never reduces the required minimum in any event.

The rider's own track corroborates her account: 88 qualifying rider fixes, every one of them inside the 200 m TRANSPORT_HUB presence radius (maximum 91.7 m from the pin, mean 72.1 m) and stationary from 07:43:10 to 07:52:00. I do not put POL-NS-04 forward as a ground of decision — she sent no locating message during the waiting window, so limb (a) is not met — but the presence radius that clause sets shows a rider at the bay looking for a car that was not in front of her, and POL-NS-06 decides the fee whether she was there or not.

On the chat record, which I disclose is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with the issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE: both driver messages (MSG-00209-002 at 07:38:40 and MSG-00209-003 at 07:44:20) and the system arrival notification carry read_at null, which is consistent with the rider's statement that she saw nothing until afterwards. Nothing in that log supplies the missing 64 seconds — the last message falls at 07:44:20 with 230 seconds of qualifying hold still to run — and the deciding fact, the corrected dwell, does not rest on this artifact.

The disputed $6.00 is already in the rider's hands: the fare breakdown shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd of 6.00, and the 6.00 equals the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00), so the ledger itself is not in defect. Leaving the present state alone under POL-GEN-03 therefore leaves the rider refunded, which is what this evidence supports; the driver's request would require the platform to claw back a fee that POL-NS-01 does not permit it to charge.

Driver compensation under POL-NS-07 is unavailable: the clause is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and both limb (b) and limb (c) of that clause fail on the driver's own trace, so the anti-farming check is never reached. POL-NS-06 states the consequence for this branch directly — no driver compensation is payable.

claims.text: The driver reached the pickup point on clean telemetry: EV-GPS-00209 carries 108 fixes at a 10 s cadence with 100% coverage, and 25 of those fixes sit inside the 150 m arrival radius for a TRANSPORT_HUB bay, so there is no basis for any finding that the driver never came to the pickup point.

The driver used the no-show protocol rather than abandoning the trip: the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 07:38:05, shows no boarding event, and shows the trip terminated by the driver at 07:48:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 - and there is no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission anywhere in the record.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04: limb (a) of that clause requires at least one locating or coordinating message from the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log contains only the system 'driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages - the rider sent nothing at all, so her account that she 'looked for the car' never entered the in-app channel. I disclose that EV-CHAT-00209 is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (read receipts null); that issue goes to whether the driver's messages were opened, not to whether a rider message exists, and the finding that none does survives the discount.

The contact duty that POL-NS-04(b) measures was discharged on the driver's side: the system arrival notice went out at 07:38:06, the driver messaged the rider at 07:38:40 and again at 07:44:20, and both messages show delivered timestamps - so there is no failure of reply anywhere in the log, and the 120 second reply test is never even triggered because the rider sent no message. EV-CHAT-00209 is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue UNREAD_MESSAGE, which I disclose; the impairment concerns read receipts on the driver's messages, and delivery is affirmatively recorded and untouched by it.

The rider's own track shows her device stationary at 0.0 km/h across 88 fixes from 07:43:10 to 07:52:00, never further than 91.7 m from the pickup pin and therefore well inside the 200 m rider-presence radius for TRANSPORT_HUB: she was on scene and reachable throughout the window, and no artifact in this bundle corroborates her statement that no car was there to be found.

The facts that decide this case come from an unimpaired artifact: EV-GPS-00209 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, with a 10 s cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0, both tracks present and the arrival marker one second from a fix, so no limb of POL-NS-08 (a) to (d) is engaged and the POL-NS-08 escalation sentence does not apply. The IMPAIRED tag on EV-CHAT-00209 is a POL-GEN-02 down-weight only: message ids run 001 to 003 unbroken, the log holds all 3 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records, and no gap over 5 minutes spans the arrival marker, so POL-NS-08(c) is not made out by either party.

The sum in dispute is the sum this trip generated: the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) is SGD 6.00, so the fare ledger reconciles under the resolution rule and no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists.

No abuse finding attaches to this driver and no escalation ground is open on the profiles: 3 no-show terminations in 30 days across 88 completed trips is 3.4%, below both POL-NS-07 limbs (4 or more, and a ratio above 0.08), the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and neither party shows any disputes_with_counterparty_90d, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged and this case is decidable on the merits rather than held.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival machinery is not engaged on this record: the derived arrival facts publish no distance between the driver and the pin at the 07:38:05 marker and no speed at that instant, and I do not compute geometry myself, so the record does not establish that the marker was set more than 300 m out or while the driver was travelling at 15 km/h or above, and no false-arrival entry belongs in the referrals list.

I concede the dwell point rather than stretch it: the longest qualifying in-geofence run on the driver's own trace is 236 seconds, running from 07:44:14 to the 07:48:10 cancellation, which is 64 seconds short of the 300 second TRANSPORT_HUB minimum under POL-NS-01(c); the first qualifying in-geofence fix is 369 seconds after the 'arrived' marker, so limb (b)'s at-or-before requirement is not met either, and the trip record's 10.1 minute wait_time is measured from a marker the clause does not accept. On the derived figures the driver cannot bring himself within POL-NS-01 in full, and the shortfall provision in POL-NS-06 governs.

EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT: no advisory records a kerb restriction, enforcement operation, closure or accident at this bay in this window. I cite the absence only to record that the POL-NS-06(i) interval-summing route is unavailable to either side, and the driver does not rely on it.

ruling.explanation: Your two accounts agree on more than either of you allows, and the numbers decide it. Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee is chargeable only if, among other things, the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous 300 seconds - the TRANSPORT_HUB minimum - and that clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00209, COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 108 fixes at a 10 s cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0, both tracks present) credits a single qualifying hold of 236 seconds, opening 07:44:14 and ending when the driver cancelled at 07:48:10 - 64 seconds short of the 300 second minimum. The trip record's 10.1 minute wait is measured from the 07:38:05 arrival marker, which POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05 do not accept as starting the clock: the first qualifying fix is 369 seconds after that marker, so dwell_start_offset_sec of -369 confirms the run opens at 07:44:14. Limb (b) fails too, because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix at or before 07:38:05. POL-NS-06 therefore governs: the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, with no driver compensation payable, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. Accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) does not rescue the driver - the trace shows one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to sum, and the required traffic advisory is absent (EV-ADVIS-00209-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) - and POL-NS-06(ii) confirms an advisory would never lower the minimum in any event. POL-NS-05's false-arrival machinery is not made out either way: the record publishes no distance or speed at the 07:38:05 marker, so a false-arrival referral does not fire, and in any case qualifying in-geofence fixes do exist in the trip. The SGD 6.00 is in fact already refunded: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00209) records payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 6.00, and 6.00 is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so the ledger reconciles and no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists. This dispute is driver-filed, so the outcome is party-relative: NO_ACTION means the present state stands and the rider remains refunded. The fee is not restored, and the drivers' request to claw it back is refused. On the rider's side, POL-NS-04 does not apply - she sent no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window, so limb (a) is unmet - but it changes nothing, because POL-NS-06 refunds the fee on the shortfall alone. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00209) is down-weighted to 0.85 with issue UNREAD_MESSAGE: both driver messages and the system notice carry null read receipts, consistent with the rider's account that she saw nothing until afterwards. It does not carry the deciding dwell fact, so it does not cap confidence, and it supplies no extra seconds - the 64 second shortfall still stood 230 seconds after the last message at 07:44:20. On POL-NS-07, compensation is unavailable because it is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full; the anti-farming check is never reached (3 no-show terminations in 30 days across 88 completed trips, 3.4%, below both the '4 or more' and the 'above 0.08' thresholds), and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0. No escalation ground under POL-NS-09 is open, so the case is decided on the merits at confidence 0.95, above the 0.70 floor.

ruling.explanation: Both of you are looking at the same central fact, and the platform's telemetry confirms it: before cancelling, the driver held position inside the Tampines PHV bay geofence for only 236 seconds, against the 300-second minimum the no-show policy sets for a TRANSPORT_HUB pickup (POL-NS-01(c), applied through POL-NS-06). The 'arrived' marker at 07:38:05 does not start that clock — dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, which the trace puts at 07:44:14, 369 seconds after the marker — so the trip record's 10.1-minute wait is measured from a marker the policy does not accept. There is also no qualifying in-geofence fix at or before the marker (the first is at 07:44:14), so POL-NS-01(b) fails as well, and the termination at 07:48:10 came before the required 300 seconds had elapsed, so limb (d) is not made out either. With POL-NS-01 unsatisfied, POL-NS-06 governs: the $6.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable. The $6.00 is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so the fare ledger reconciles and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Driver: your request to restore the fee is not supported. The full refund has already been issued — the fare breakdown shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd of $6.00 — so the present state stands and nothing further moves; the ruling is NO_ACTION, which leaves the rider refunded. ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the decisive numbers, and the record confirms them. A no-show cancellation fee is chargeable only if the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for at least 300 seconds (the TRANSPORT_HUB minimum in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec), and the clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap (POL-NS-01(c)).

The driver's 'arrived' event is at 07:38:05 (EV-TRIP-00209) and he cancelled at 07:48:10, which is why the trip record shows a wait of 10.1 minutes. But the driver's own trace (EV-GPS-00209, COMPLETE, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, max gap 0 s) shows the longest uninterrupted in-geofence hold is 236 seconds, opening at 07:44:14 and closed by the cancellation at 07:48:10 — 369 seconds after the marker. That is 64 seconds short of the 300-second minimum, and the first qualifying in-geofence fix is likewise 369 seconds after the marker, so there is no in-radius fix at or before the arrival tap.

Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 therefore fails, and with it the clause. POL-NS-06 then governs: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum, the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded. The interval-summing route in POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable: the trace shows a single in-geofence run (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add, and EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so there is no advisory that could permit summing. POL-NS-06(ii) confirms an advisory could never reduce the minimum in any case.

Driver compensation under POL-NS-07 is not payable: it is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check is never reached (3 no-show terminations in 30 days across 88 trips, 3.4%, below both limbs of that test). POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral does not fire — limb (ii) requires no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere, and 25 exist.

The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00209) reconciles: the $6.00 fee equals the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the $6.00 has already been refunded to the rider (refund_issued_sgd 6.00, payment_status REFUNDED).

On the rider's side, POL-NS-04 does not apply: she sent no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window, so limb (a) fails. Her GPS track confirms she was on scene (88 fixes, all within the 200 m presence radius, maximum 91.7 m), but that does not change the dwell analysis, and the driver's dispute does not turn on her presence.

The chat log (EV-CHAT-00209) is down-weighted to 0.85 with issue UNREAD_MESSAGE — all three messages carry read_at null, consistent with the rider's account that she saw nothing until afterwards. The deciding fact, the corrected dwell, does not rest on it, so the impairment does not lower confidence.

The outcome for the driver's filing is that the fee was not chargeable, so the $6.00 already returned to the rider stands. In the vocabulary of POL-GEN-03 this is NO_ACTION: the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state is left as it is, which on a driver-filed dispute over a fee already reversed means the rider remains refunded. No money moves to the driver — there is no refund to the filing party and no compensation. No clause produces a referral, and no POL-NS-09 escalation ground is met: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, there is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts, neither party shows a repeat dispute between the pair, the anti-farming check does not trip, and the deciding fact rests on artifacts unimpaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d).
